People, city and archaeological culture

Pensacola/Panzacola is a historical people-name associated with Pensacola Bay in West Florida. The initial reading path now points to original people-specific research and distinguishes this name from the later city and the broader archaeological Pensacola culture.

Read the sources [1] University of West Florida — Patrick Anthony DeRoche

02

A focused source, with limits

DeRoche’s thesis examines documentary and archaeological evidence for the historical Panzacola. The introduction and selected pages support this initial orientation; they do not establish a positively identified excavated village. The remaining thesis, contemporary descendant connections and other original accounts need further review.

Read the sources [1] University of West Florida — Patrick Anthony DeRoche

What needs further research

  • Build a people-specific reading collection beyond the selected thesis passages; compare original documentary accounts and descendant/community histories.
  • The title page and repository cover differ in year. Neither a later city name nor archaeological ceramics alone establishes a people’s identity.

Academic / referenceUniversity of West Florida — Patrick Anthony DeRocheSource 1Supporting reference · outside substantive inspected count

Patrick Anthony DeRoche — In Pursuit of the Panzacola: A Historical Documentary and Archaeological Investigation ↗

DeRoche’s introduction explicitly places the historical Panzacola people around present-day Pensacola Bay in West Florida using seventeenth-century documentary accounts. His discussion distinguishes this people from the archaeological Pensacola culture; the test excavation did not establish a positive Panzacola site identification. Inspection: Actual university public download, valid-TLS HTTP 200, 2,675,875 bytes, 100 PDF pages including added cover. Cover/title; abstract printed p.viii / PDF p.9; introduction printed pp.1–3 / PDF pp.10–12; and printed p.8 / PDF p.17 were read as text/OCR. Not a complete thesis or excavation-data review. Limits: The canonical name Pensacola is retained; Panzacola is the historical people-label used by the thesis. The later city and archaeological culture are separate referents. No definitive excavated Panzacola village, coordinates, ethnicity-from-ceramics inference, contemporary recognition status or disappearance claim is adopted. This is an original student thesis with committee oversight, not a statement of consensus on every historical identification.
